description: Finish productizing clawctl distribution: verified release workflow, Linux secret backend, stable --json output, command-based MCP server, clawctl init bootstrap, plugin marketplace registration, and a v0.1.0 release prep.

No other file in the repo references install/clawctl.rb

userStories.title: Portable secret backend for Linux (CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD)
userStories.description: As a Linux user, I want to authenticate without macOS Keychain so I can use the same binary on a Linux dev box or CI runner.
acceptanceCriteria: On Linux (runtime.GOOS == 'linux'), internal/keychain resolves the token by trying in order: CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD (exec, capture stdout, trim whitespace), secret-tool lookup service openclaw-gateway-token account $USER, pass show openclaw/gateway-token
If all three fail, the error message names all three options and how to set them
On macOS, the existing 'security find-generic-password' path is unchanged
CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD is also honored on macOS when set (override path)
CLAWCTL_TOKEN env var is NOT added as a token source (design principle #2)
docs/auth.md is created with one-paragraph setup recipes for: macOS Keychain, CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD, secret-tool, pass
Unit tests cover: macOS keychain path, Linux CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD path, Linux all-backends-fail (error text check), macOS override via CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Document and freeze the exit-code contract
userStories.description: As an agent author, I want every exit code documented so I can branch on them deterministically without reverse-engineering the binary.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/cli-contract.md is created listing exit codes 0, 2, 6, 7, 22, 28 with the precise condition that produces each
clawctl --help (or the default no-args output) includes a one-line pointer: 'Exit codes: see docs/cli-contract.md'
README.md 'Exit codes' table (if it exists) is replaced with a link to docs/cli-contract.md rather than a duplicate table

A test in cmd/clawctl/ asserts each documented exit code is emitted for a representative failure: usage error (2), DNS failure (6), connection refused (7), HTTP 4xx (22), timeout (28) — use a mock transport to simulate each
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Stable --json output mode across read commands
userStories.description: As an agent author, I want clawctl health, models, msg, verify, and trace to emit a stable JSON envelope when --json is passed so I can parse output without scraping prose.
acceptanceCriteria: --json global flag (or CLAWCTL_OUTPUT=json env var) is accepted by all five subcommands: health, models, msg, verify, trace
Each command emits exactly one JSON object on stdout: {"command": "<name>", "ok": true|false, "data": {...}, "error": null | {"code": "<string>", "message": "<string>", "trace_id": "<string>"}}
For msg, data wraps the existing ToolResponse fields (agent, finish_reason, usage, content, redactions)
Redaction is applied to data and error.message before output
Trace-id continues to be written to stderr even when --json is set
docs/cli-contract.md (created in US-004) is updated with the data shape and a JSON example for each command
Unit tests assert the envelope shape for each command: one happy-path and one error-path case per command
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: clawctl mcp — document guard rails for mutating ops
userStories.description: As a security-conscious user, I want it clearly documented that cli is not exposed over MCP in v0.x, with a note on how any future opt-in must look.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/mcp.md has a 'Security' section explaining why cli is excluded: 'mutating SSH-driven ops require a human in the loop; expose them only after explicit --unsafe-mutating opt-in'
internal/mcpserver/server.go has a comment at the tool-registration site noting that any future mutating tool must be guarded by an --unsafe-mutating flag
Reading cmd/clawctl/mcp.go confirms no path registers or calls the cli subcommand
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Redesign MCP server: command-based tools (health, models, verify, trace)
userStories.description: As an MCP client user, I want clawctl mcp to expose clawctl's read-only commands as typed MCP tools instead of exposing one tool per openclaw agent, so I can call health, models, verify, and trace directly.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/mcpserver is refactored: add BuildCommandServer(impl *Implementation, src TokenSource, baseURL string) (*mcp.Server, error) that registers static command-based tools (no /v1/models fetch at startup)
Four tools are registered: clawctl_health, clawctl_models, clawctl_verify, clawctl_trace
clawctl_health: no required inputs; handler calls GET /health via internal/transport/api and returns JSON response body as tool result content
clawctl_models: no required inputs; handler calls GET /v1/models via internal/transport/api (or cache) and returns the JSON body
clawctl_verify: required input 'type' (enum: commit|pr|issue|file), required 'ref' (string), optional 'path' (string); handler delegates to the same logic as cmd/clawctl/verify.go
clawctl_trace: required input 'trace_id' (string); handler delegates to the same logic as cmd/clawctl/trace.go
cmd/clawctl/mcp.go is updated to call BuildCommandServer; the old Build(agents) path is removed
tools/list returns exactly {clawctl_health, clawctl_models, clawctl_verify, clawctl_trace} — no agent tools, no clawctl_msg yet (added in US-008)
Unit tests: tools/list shape, one round-trip per tool against a mock transport returning fixture JSON
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add clawctl_msg tool to MCP server
userStories.description: As an MCP client user, I want to call clawctl_msg from an MCP tool so I can send a prompt to any openclaw agent and get a typed ToolResponse back.
acceptanceCriteria: clawctl_msg tool is added to the command server (BuildCommandServer from US-007)
Input schema: required 'agent' (string, openclaw agent slug e.g. 'concierge'), required 'text' (string, minLength 1), optional 'session_id' (string), optional 'tool_choice' (enum: auto|none|required)
Handler calls POST /v1/chat/completions (non-streaming) via internal/transport/api and wraps the result in a ToolResponse envelope
Redaction is applied to the response before it is returned to the MCP client
tools/list now returns exactly {clawctl_health, clawctl_models, clawctl_verify, clawctl_trace, clawctl_msg}
docs/mcp.md is updated with a worked example: the claude mcp add registration command and a clawctl_msg tool call snippet
Unit test: one round-trip against a mock transport returning a chat completions fixture, assert ToolResponse shape in tool result content
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Bootstrap helper (clawctl init)
userStories.description: As a new user, I want one command that prints platform-correct setup snippets and can verify my configuration is working.
acceptanceCriteria: clawctl init detects runtime.GOOS and prints copy-pasteable setup snippets: on macOS, security add-generic-password Keychain command; on Linux, CLAWCTL_TOKEN_CMD / secret-tool / pass instructions
Output goes to stdout; ANSI color codes are suppressed when stdout is not a tty (use os.Stdout.Fd() + term.IsTerminal or equivalent)

clawctl init --check runs three checks in sequence: (1) CLAWCTL_HOST is non-empty, (2) token resolver returns a non-empty token, (3) GET /health returns HTTP 200; exits 0 only if all three pass, exits 2 with per-check result if any fail
clawctl init --check uses the real token resolver (internal/keychain) and real HTTP transport, so it validates the actual environment
Unit tests use a mock token source and mock HTTP transport to cover: all checks pass, CLAWCTL_HOST unset, token resolver fails, health HTTP 500
clawctl init is added to cmd/clawctl/main.go dispatch and mentioned in clawctl --help
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Linux smoke test in CI
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want test/smoke.sh to run syntax-clean on Linux in CI so a Linux regression is caught on every PR.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a job 'smoke-static' to .github/workflows/ci.yml running on ubuntu-latest
Job runs: bash -n test/smoke.sh (syntax check) and shellcheck test/smoke.sh (lint)
Add --no-network flag to test/smoke.sh: when present (or when CLAWCTL_HOST is unset), skip every test that requires a live gateway and exit 0
Existing live-gateway tests are guarded by a check that exits early when --no-network or CLAWCTL_HOST is unset, printing 'skipping live tests (no CLAWCTL_HOST set)'
CONTRIBUTING.md gets a 'Running smoke tests' section: how to run with --no-network locally and what is needed for the full live suite
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: install.sh post-release smoke test in CI
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want CI to prove install.sh can install a real release artifact on both macOS and Linux, so a resolver regression is caught before users hit it.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a job 'install-smoke' to .github/workflows/ci.yml with matrix [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]
Job uses CLAWCTL_INSTALL_DIR pointing at a temp dir (no sudo) and runs bash install/install.sh
Job asserts: $CLAWCTL_INSTALL_DIR/clawctl version exits 0 and output contains 'clawctl'
Job asserts: $CLAWCTL_INSTALL_DIR/clawctl --help exits 0
Job skips gracefully when no published release exists: check via gh release list --limit 1; if empty, print 'no release published yet, skipping' and exit 0
bash -n install/install.sh and shellcheck install/install.sh still pass (existing regression check)
Typecheck passes
